sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. viii+187 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not cover the Rai Coast languages at all (Ganglau, Yaganon absent); its only stress remark (p. ~4) is that stress marking was omitted for the Madang-district languages it treats because 'the stress patterning has not been well established yet'. Not applicable to Ganglau.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.4.2 (p. 61) gives Ganglau's location, 200 speakers and a divergent Dumun-Kulilau dialect. Sec. 6.1.1 (p. 63) sketches Yaganon-family phonology (stop/nasal series, word-initial velar nasal 'observed in Ganglau', syllabic velar nasals, l/r, [h]~[s] correspondences) with no mention of stress. The syllable paragraph on p. 66 says 'In the Yaganon Family syllables may be closed by voiceless stops, p, t, k, voiced stops b, d, g, and nasals m, n and ng'; its only stress remarks are about Rawa, Yupna, Wantoat and Suroi, none about Yaganon/Ganglau.
Sole lexical source for Ganglau is Z'graggen (1980); no phonology or stress notes.
